sentences.text: 1 4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant was in the friendship with the victim as they are willing to enter into marriage but due to some misunderstanding F.I.R. of the case in question was lodged and appellant is ready to enter into marriage with the victim within three months from the date of release.

He further submits that Investigating Officer filed the charge sheet in mechanical manner and the court below also failed to appreciate the evidences in correct perspective and passed the impugned order.

He further submits that there is no possibility of tampering of any evidence, therefore, appellant, who is in jail since 15.07.2023, is entitled for bail and the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

5. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the complainant vehemently oppose the prayer of the appellant and submit that on the pretext of marriage appellant made physical relations with the victim and thereafter, he denied to enter into marriage.
They also submit that the gravity of the offence will not overcome, in case, appellant solemnize marriage with the victim, therefore, there is no illegality in the impugned order.

6. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant-applicant, learned A.G.A., learned counsel for the complainant and going through the contents of the appeal, impugned order, F.I.R., counter affidavit filed by learned A.G.A., rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for the appellant, it is evident that on the pretext of marriage, appellant made physical relations with the victim and now appellant is ready to solemnize marriage with the victim.
7. In view of above facts and circumstances, this Court is of the view that impugned order is bad in the eye of law, therefore, the appeal is allowed.

8. Order dated 19.09.2023 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act/Additional District & Session Judge,
Court No.2, Unnao in Bail Application No. 2860 of 2023 arising out of F.I.R. No. 149 of 2023, under Sections 376 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, P.S. Bihar, District Unnao, is hereby set aside.
9. Let appellant Shiv Shankar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.25,000/- and two reliable sureties each of the like amount subject to following additional conditions :-
(i) The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he will not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through their counsel.
